children: Singapore's exports growth in October smashed expectations, setting a fresh multi-decade high amid continued demand for goods tied to artificial intelligence.
Non-oil domestic exports last month surged 79.8% compared with the same period a year earlier, beating September's already impressive 68.3% increase and eclipsing economists' expectations.
Forecasters had widely expected to see a slowdown in trade figures at the start of the fourth quarter, with a poll by LSEG tipping an expansion of 37.7%.
The better-than-anticipated print brings year-to-date growth in exports to 33.6%, signaling that Singapore is on track for one of its best trade performances in recent memory.
The reading marks a 24th consecutive month of NODX expansion and the eighth straight month of double-digit growth, according to OCBC economists.
Blockbuster exports growth bodes well for the small, open economy, helping offset the drag from external headwinds stemming from the war in the Middle East and lingering concerns around tariffs.

Singapore doesn't occupy the same sort of role in the AI supply chain as chip-making powerhouses like South Korea and Taiwan, but has benefited from the buildout of AI infrastructure thanks to its position as a hub for integrated circuits, chip-making equipment and related components.

In its most recent regional outlook report, the International Monetary Fund raised Singapore's economic growth forecast for this year by 1.5 percentage points to 5.0%, in part due to the AI spillover effect.
October's trade data showed that the AI tailwind is still in full force, with electronics exports rising 73.9% on year, compared with September's 107.6% increase.
Non-electronics exports did even better, gaining 73.9% compared with a 54.1% increase the prior month.
The U.S., China and the EU were top destinations for Singapore goods during October, with exports to all three markets growing strongly, data from Enterprise Singapore showed.
